key_insight: The paper argues that AI/ML for turbulence works best when matched to the flow’s complexity regime, not applied generically across all turbulent flows.
engineering_relevance: A flow-aware turbulence taxonomy can help engineers choose between ML-RANS, scale-resolving simulation, and PINNs more effectively, avoiding both overuse and misuse of expensive models.
method: Map turbulence using two axes: Reynolds number (Re) and non-equilibrium level (Sk/ε).
Apply Weaver’s complexity framework to classify flows into distinct physical regimes.
Use the regime map to identify where ML-RANS can generalize, where explicit scale resolution is required, and where PINNs are most suitable.
evidence_signal: The abstract synthesizes prior AI/ML turbulence experience and reports that ML-RANS often fails to generalize while SRS is computationally prohibitive, motivating the proposed taxonomy rather than presenting new simulation data.
watch_item: The framework is conceptual and depends on correctly identifying the flow regime; using a model outside its domain of validity can still lead to poor predictions.
paper_title: AI Meets Turbulence Modeling: Complex Systems Perspective
